records.limitation: One application and change, approximate token counting and incomplete refactoring-cost accounting; this does not establish general ROI or savings for every future task.

records.label: TDD inside the agent loop - theater or actual value?
records.summary: Separates human-authored tests, a human review checkpoint and TDD entirely inside an agent loop. The small exploratory comparison found no clear advantage for fully internal TDD in model-judged quality or mutation scores.
records.limitation: Small greenfield tasks, imperfect adherence and an LLM-defined quality rubric. Reported aggregate tokens include cache rereads and are not equivalent to billed cost; no universal conclusion about human-led TDD follows.

records.label: Are Harnesses Worth the Cost?
records.summary: Compares development with and without a behavioral harness against a separate acceptance suite. On the selected service, the stronger model passed both conditions; a cost-optimized model passed more consistently with harness feedback, at greater per-attempt effort.
records.limitation: Ten paired runs per model on one unusually detailed greenfield Java brief. Guides and sensors changed together; estimated generation costs omit harness authoring, review and repairs. Final-gate-only use is proposed, not tested.

records.label: When Software Meets Hardware
records.summary: An IoT modernization account connects physical test environments, device simulation, observability, recovery and continuous learning. The team used LLMs to explore unfamiliar areas, prototype experiments and develop engineering tools, including dashboards and migration trackers. The proposed benefit is cheaper experimentation and a shorter learning loop.
records.limitation: The article describes one team's practices and perceived benefits. It does not isolate AI's contribution or quantify productivity improvements. Physical-world validation remains part of the reported engineering process.
